reviewer: Claude (maintainer-requested fix of the advisory recheck base)
summary: threat-review.yml rechecked PR evidence with --base HEAD, i.e. the default-branch head it checks out. That head moves; when the PR is merged before the workflow_run starts (PR #78: merged 16:08:27, run 16:09:09) it contains the PR, the merge-base becomes the PR head and the record is reported stale. The recheck and the delta advisory now use the PR base commit from the event (workflow_run.pull_requests[0].base.sha), validated as a 40-hex SHA, passed only through an environment variable (no expression interpolation into the script), fetched by SHA like the head; a missing base fails with an explicit message. The base value comes from GitHub, not from the candidate; fork and Dependabot runs remain skipped by the job condition, permissions stay contents:read. Weekly/manual full reviews still use HEAD, which is correct there. A selftest reproduces the merged case and a workflow test guards against reintroducing --base HEAD.

findings.evidence: Run 42249662135 (Threat model advisory, PR #78): 'Stale base_sha' and 'Stale change_digest' because the default-branch checkout already contained the merged PR.
findings.resolution: Recheck and delta advisory use the PR base SHA from the workflow_run event; regression tests added.

tests.evidence: Ran 20 tests, OK (new: merged PR against own base, workflow uses PR base)
No router or agent code changed

limitations: The workflow_run path itself runs only in GitHub Actions after a PR's CI; it is verified by reading, YAML parsing and the static workflow test, and will first run for real on the next PR after this one is merged.
The trusted workflow comes from the default branch, so this PR's own advisory run still uses the old --base HEAD and may show the false failure once more.
